questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not require the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers that a passenger is on board.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat large enough for two riders. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be ready for:

options.text: Empty parking spaces.
A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to suddenly pull out into traffic. It is safest to ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space to avoid danger.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that cover your ankles give the best protection. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in safely before riding.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever feels comfortable, no matter the safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs to stay safe while riding.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: Your normal search routine should include:

options.text: Frequent head checks.
Frequent body checks.
Turning your entire body to look around.
Keeping your eyes only on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent head checks.
questions.explanation: Make frequent head checks part of your normal routine. You must know what is happening around you at all times to stay safe.

questions.question: Night riding is usually:

options.text: Easier than day riding because you can see other vehicle lights better.
Harder than day riding because it is harder to see.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than day riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than day riding because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as easily. Without normal shadows and light, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: When possible, change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: By the left handgrip
By the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually near the left handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What is it called when you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Engine braking.
Acceleration.
Upshifting.
Coasting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like braking does. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks full.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before riding. A tire that is not full enough may still look okay, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not use your mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well back from the vehicle in front of you, even when both of you are stopped. This gives you room to move if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes toward you too fast from behind.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a motorcycle you don't know?

options.text: Check that the seat feels comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally since all bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Be careful with a new motorcycle. Learn how it works before you ride. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes, and learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is allowed?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done in areas where passing is legal and safe. You must stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: In a no passing zone, can a motorcycle pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, a motorcycle may still pass.
No, a motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
Yes, if the pass finishes before another vehicle approaches.
Yes, if the motorcycle passes on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, a motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your plans hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes less well than eyeglasses.
Nothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not good enough to replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When you must ride over an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Turn the wheel quickly.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it straight on. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright and rise off your seat so your knees absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting it, roll the throttle a little to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you change lanes.
To take attention away from your vehicle.
To show that an exit is coming.
To ask other drivers to let you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal or hand signal every time you turn or change lanes. Turn it off after your turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the emergency brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This includes regular stops, not just emergencies.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Do not ride.
Ride if you feel fine, even after drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not ride.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet has all of the following except:

options.text: A hard outer shell to resist impact.
An inner padding that absorbs impact.
A chin strap to keep it in place.
Bright paint colors on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright paint colors on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have a hard outer shell, inner padding, comfort liner, and chin strap. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking sound.
The brakes create friction with the steering.
Each brake can stop and hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop and hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop and hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during the day, it is important to:

options.text: Avoid riding during the day.
Wear bright clothing when riding.
Wear sunglasses when riding.
Ride on the shoulder as much as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing when riding.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day.
